testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps you keep control of your vehicle during hard braking. It does not make your vehicle stop faster.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor.
The amount of air pressure needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.
questions.explanation: Air takes time to flow through the brake lines. There is usually at least a half-second delay between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes begin working. This delay is called brake lag.

questions.question: If spring brakes activate while you are hauling a heavy load, stopping will:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all wheels. If they activate due to low air pressure, your vehicle will need a longer distance to stop, especially when carrying a heavy load.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than ____ psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 5 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster than this, something needs to be repaired before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear and use engine braking.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only when needed to help slow down.

questions.question: How do Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) work with other braking systems?

options.text: They reduce your vehicle's braking power.
They work with other brakes and do not reduce braking power.
They do not work well on large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work with other brakes and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works together with your normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease your braking power. ABS only activates when your wheels are about to lock up.

questions.question: In an emergency stop, how should you brake?

options.text: Swerve your trailer to the right and stop.
Swerve your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, keep your vehicle in a straight line. This helps you stay in control and still allows you to steer if needed.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other braking systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained properly, air brakes are safe and effective for stopping large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: Where should a front brake limiting valve be set for normal stopping power?
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Keep the valve set to "normal" for full stopping power. Setting it to "slippery" reduces your stopping power.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.explanation: Do not push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force of the springs and air pressure can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: ABS malfunction lamps are yellow. Even if the ABS is not working, you still have regular braking power.

questions.question: When air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
Begin pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air when tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, it:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, switch into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Switch to a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will increase your speed, and a low gear helps you control the vehicle.

questions.question: You must have an air brake endorsement to:

options.text: Operate a vehicle with air brakes.
Drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Operate a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes test to get a license to drive a vehicle with air brakes, including air over hydraulic systems.

questions.question: Alcohol evaporators are:

options.text: Used to add alcohol to brake systems to prevent freezing.
Only allowed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used to add alcohol to brake systems to prevent freezing.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming, which can damage brakes.

questions.question: Test the low pressure warning signal by:

options.text: Turning on the engine and applying the trailer hand brake.
Rapidly pressing and releasing the brake pedal.
Removing wheel chocks and disengaging the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rapidly pressing and releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: After the system charges, rapidly press and release the brake pedal to test the warning signal. This releases air, and the warning should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal is:

options.text: Not required on vehicles with air brakes.
Required on vehicles with air brakes.
Optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If it goes off while driving, stop completely and have the system repaired.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator is most important in:
questions.explanation: Alcohol evaporators are important in cold weather. They add alcohol to the brake system to prevent ice from forming.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute. This is the safe leakage limit during a leakage test.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used to:

options.text: Make the air brakes work more effectively.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank allows you to temporarily release the spring brakes in an emergency. If the spring brakes activate due to low air pressure, you can push the proper control to release them briefly and move the vehicle.

questions.question: In an S-cam brake, friction happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created when the brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. Both the emergency brake and parking brake use mechanical force.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and oil. These can damage the system if they build up. Air tank drain valves help remove water and oil from the system.
